paras.text: Presenting by simulating the characteristics of something. For example, walking like a lame person — acting — is its best example. Some real thing, condition, matter or process is simulated so that some result or information may be derived. Presenting the behaviour or characteristics of some physical or imaginary system for learning. Simulation is used in many respects, for example for safety, for testing, for recreation, for training or for education etc. Natural systems or the human system etc. are presented by simulating them in the form of scientific models so that detailed knowledge about these things may be obtained, for example the model of a globe or the solar system. Simulation is done when access to the real thing is impossible or presenting it in its real state is difficult, e.g. the sun cannot be seen in its real state. In the social sciences simulation is generally used for training. For example, simulating the elections of the National Assembly in school so that children may understand this process well.

Learning Through Simulation

Presenting by simulating the characteristics of something. For example, walking like a lame person — acting — is its best example. Some real thing, condition, matter or process is simulated so that some result or information may be derived. Presenting the behaviour or characteristics of some physical or imaginary system for learning. Simulation is used in many respects, for example for safety, for testing, for recreation, for training or for education etc. Natural systems or the human system etc. are presented by simulating them in the form of scientific models so that detailed knowledge about these things may be obtained, for example the model of a globe or the solar system. Simulation is done when access to the real thing is impossible or presenting it in its real state is difficult, e.g. the sun cannot be seen in its real state. In the social sciences simulation is generally used for training. For example, simulating the elections of the National Assembly in school so that children may understand this process well.

In learning through simulation some difficulties or problems also come forward, for example first obtaining correct information about that thing so that its behaviour and characteristics may be presented exactly; giving growth and simple form to assumptions and estimates in simulation; then the status and importance of the information obtained.

The process of learning through simulation plays an important role in training. Its purpose is to prepare people for expected tragedies. In it some accident is presented artificially and it is seen what the reaction of the learner is and what it should be. In this kind of simulation training is given in what should be done in terrorist attacks; how natural disasters should be dealt with; what should be done if chaos arises, or other such events in which there are dangers to life — what should be done.

Events taking place in the real world cannot be shown once again. This is why in institutions students are given such training through simulation that they become able to play an active role in practical life outside the classroom or institution. Most institutions, to save their employees from possible accidents of this kind, provide them training through mock activities …

Learning Through Simulation

Presenting by simulating the characteristics of something. For example, walking like a lame person — acting — is its best example. Some real thing, condition, matter or process is simulated so that some result or information may be derived. Presenting the behaviour or characteristics of some physical or imaginary system for learning. Simulation is used in many respects, for example for safety, for testing, for recreation, for training or for education etc. Natural systems or the human system etc. are presented by simulating them in the form of scientific models so that detailed knowledge about these things may be obtained, for example the model of a globe or the solar system. Simulation is done when access to the real thing is impossible or presenting it in its real state is difficult, e.g. the sun cannot be seen in its real state. In the social sciences simulation is generally used for training. For example, simulating the elections of the National Assembly in school so that children may understand this process well.

In learning through simulation some difficulties or problems also come forward, for example first obtaining correct information about that thing so that its behaviour and characteristics may be presented exactly; giving growth and simple form to assumptions and estimates in simulation; then the status and importance of the information obtained.

The process of learning through simulation plays an important role in training. Its purpose is to prepare people for expected tragedies. In it some accident is presented artificially and it is seen what the reaction of the learner is and what it should be. In this kind of simulation training is given in what should be done in terrorist attacks; how natural disasters should be dealt with; what should be done if chaos arises, or other such events in which there are dangers to life — what should be done.

Events taking place in the real world cannot be shown once again. This is why in institutions students are given such training through simulation that they become able to play an active role in practical life outside the classroom or institution. paras.text: In the General Assembly of the United Nations all member countries have representation, and every country has the right of one vote. Every year a regular session of the Assembly is held. This session begins in the month of September on the day of the third Tuesday and generally concludes by Christmas. If the Security Council or a majority of its members files a request, special sessions of the Assembly can also be summoned. Every year a President and seventeen Vice-Presidents of the General Assembly are elected. The General Assembly is authorised to debate any subject. It can present recommendations to the Security Council and the member states. Without the permission of the Council the General Assembly is not authorised to debate those matters which are under consideration in the Security Council. Activities

1. Watch the proceedings of the session of international institutions on television or the internet.

2. Hold a session on the pattern of the General Assembly / Security Council of the United Nations.

For the said activities it is necessary to know about the structure and sessions of the General Assembly and the Security Council of the United Nations.

In the General Assembly of the United Nations all member countries have representation, and every country has the right of one vote. Every year a regular session of the Assembly is held. This session begins in the month of September on the day of the third Tuesday and generally concludes by Christmas. If the Security Council or a majority of its members files a request, special sessions of the Assembly can also be summoned. Every year a President and seventeen Vice-Presidents of the General Assembly are elected. The General Assembly is authorised to debate any subject. It can present recommendations to the Security Council and the member states. Without the permission of the Council the General Assembly is not authorised to debate those matters which are under consideration in the Security Council. Accepting its recommendations is not legally necessary. The General Assembly, except for some matters, can present resolutions with a simple majority. On important matters a two-thirds majority is needed, for example the issue of world peace and order, membership of the United Nations and financial affairs etc. are important matters.

The Security Council is in fact the executive of the United Nations. It has fifteen members, of which five countries, i.e. China, America, Russia, Britain and France, are permanent members, while ten are elected by the General Assembly for two years. اقوامِ متحدہ کی جنرل اسمبلی میں تمام رکن ممالک کو نمائندگی حاصل ہے اور ہر ملک کو ایک ووٹ کا حق حاصل ہے۔ ہر سال اسمبلی کا باقاعدہ اجلاس منعقد کیا جاتا ہے۔ یہ اجلاس ستمبر کے مہینے میں تیسرے منگل کے دن سے شروع ہوتا ہے اور عام طور پر کرسمس تک اِختتام پذیر ہوتا ہے۔ سیکورٹی کونسل یا اِس کے ارکان کی اکثریت اگر درخواست دائر کرے تو اسمبلی کے خصوصی اجلاس بھی طلب کئے جا سکتے ہیں۔ ہر سال جنرل اسمبلی کے صدر اور سترہ نائب صدور کا اِنتخاب ہوتا ہے۔ جنرل اسمبلی کسی بھی موضوع پر بحث کی مجاز ہے۔ یہ سیکورٹی کونسل اور رکن ارکان کو سفارشات پیش کر سکتی ہے۔ کونسل کی اجازت کے بغیر جنرل اسمبلی اُن معاملات پر بحث کی مجاز نہیں جو سیکورٹی کونسل میں زیرِ غور ہو۔ اِن کی سفارشات کو ماننا قانونی طور پر ضروری نہیں۔ جنرل اسمبلی چند معاملات کے علاوہ سادہ اکثریت کے ساتھ قراردادیں پیش کر سکتی ہے۔ اہم معاملات پر دو تہائی اکثریت کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے۔ مثال کے طور پر عالمی امن و امان کا مسئلہ، اقوامِ متحدہ کی رکنیت اور مالی اُمور وغیرہ اہم معاملات ہیں۔
